question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{27}∼N(2,{9}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $27$ from a normal population, calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}>3).$

*Hint: A value table of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ | $\,0.7190\,$ | $\,0.7224\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ | $\,0.7517\,$ | $\,0.7549\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ | $\,0.7823\,$ | $\,0.7852\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(2,\frac{{9}^{2}}{27}) \\  & ∼N(2,3).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>3).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>3) & =P(Z>\frac{3-2}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =P(Z>0.58).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>0.58) & =1-P(Z\le 0.58) \\  & =1-Φ(0.58).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.58)=0.7190.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>3) & =1-Φ(0.58) \\  & =1-0.7190 \\  & =0.2810.\end{aligned}
$$
